sections.content:
You know *aunque* and *aun cuando* from B2 Unit 8, and the rule from B2 Unit 4: when the subject does not change, use the infinitive; when it changes, use *que* + subjunctive. This lesson adds two more ways to say that something does not stop you.

• *aun a riesgo de*: "even at the risk of". You do something knowing that something bad could follow. With the same subject, an infinitive follows: *Lo dijo aun a riesgo de perder su trabajo.* With a different subject, *que* + subjunctive follows: *Lo dijo aun a riesgo de que nadie le creyera.* The bad result is only possible, so it is never in the indicative.
• *así* + subjunctive: "even if". It works like *aunque* + subjunctive and is more common in speech: *Voy a ir, así llueva.*

items.spanish: Lo dijo aun a riesgo de perder su trabajo.
items.english: He said it even at the risk of losing his job.

items.spanish: Lo dijo aun a riesgo de que nadie le creyera.
items.english: He said it even at the risk of nobody believing him.
I am going to go, even if it rains.

items.spanish: Voy a comprarlo, así cueste mucho dinero.
items.english: I am going to buy it, even if it costs a lot of money.

sections.content: *Aun* in *aun a riesgo de* has no accent, as in *aun cuando*. And *aun a riesgo de* needs both *a* and *de*: *aun a riesgo que* and *aun riesgo de* are mistakes.
